name: H3 PDD output-head bank fusion
plain: A distilled H3 LoRA can carry several stacked output heads, one per fine training step. An actual sampler step spans several fine steps, so the output head used on that step is a dt-weighted mix of those heads. Core handles a converted bank natively; several packs instead load the official files and fuse the heads themselves, and they differ on what the stored heads mean and on which schedules they allow.
math:
Fine grid g_j on [1,0], n+1 points; d_j = differences of (1 − s·g/(1+(s−1)·g)), with s = stream shift (12 video, 3 audio).
w_j = d_j / Σ d over the fine steps inside this sampler step.
Core, _pdd_head: head = H_0 + Σ_{j≥max(start,1)} w_j·H_j (row 0 is a full head, later rows are offsets).
CineConIA, fuse_heads: head_block = Σ w_j·H_j over each block of 4, treating every row as a full head.
Deno: same weighted mean, weights from overlap of the requested σ interval with the bank's trained grid, recomputed per schedule.

props.hook: core: final layer inside the model. Packs: add_object_patch on final_layer.video_out/audio_out or final_layer.forward + DIFFUSION_MODEL wrapper
props.params: 32 fine steps, block 4, 8 sampler steps in the official files (CineConIA validates this)

label: from code
surprise: Core treats rows after the first as offsets from a full head; CineConIA's comment says the official heads are full velocities, not offsets. The two may describe different file layouts (inference: converted vs original), so a file must match the loader it goes to.
